Location2: DEPT OF ENERGY SITE - EXPLOSIVE TESTING RESEARCH FACILITY

Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: LAWRENCE LIVERMORE NATIONAL LABRATORY
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 37.634053, -121.50135 (Approximated from premise)
Report Description///THIS IS AN UPDATE TO REPORT 1402355/// THE UPDATED INFO IS AS FOLLOWS: CALLER REPORTS THAT A POTENTIALLY REPORTABLE QUANTITY OF PENTACHLOROPHENOL WAS RELEASED (GREATER THAN 10 LBS), THE TOTAL IS STILL YET TO BE DETERMINED. CALLER REPORTS THAT THEY HAVE NOT RECEIVED THE REPORT REGARDING CREOSOTE FROM THE SECONDARY LAB TESTING THE MATERIAL, SO IT IS STILL UNKNOWN IF THEY CONTAIN CREOSOTE. POWER POLES ARE BEING STORED IN CORPS YARD 834. LOCAL NEWS COVERAGE WAS INDICATED ON MEDIA INTEREST. CALOES WAS NOTIFIED AND REPORT NUMBER HAS BEEN INCLUDED THE ORIGINAL REPORTED INFO: CALLER STATES A SITE WAS IMPACTED BY A WILDFIRE AT THE INCIDENT LOCATION. A SHINGLED AWNING OF A BUILDING (830) WAS BURNED. THE MASTIC AND ROOFING SHINGLES WERE TESTED AND INDICATED IT HAVING 10% CHRYSOTILE ASBESTOS. AFTER CALCULATIONS, IT IS POSSIBLE THAT UP TO 1 POUND OF ASBESTOS BECAME FRIABLE. MOST OF THE REMNANTS OF THE ROOF, REMAIN WITHIN THE PRINT OF BUILDING 830 ON THE GROUND AND WILL BE PROPERLY MITIGATED WHEN IT IS SAFE TO DO SO. ADDITIONAL TESTING IS PENDING FOR DAMAGED CHEMICALLY TREATED UTILITY POLES AND THERE ARE NO OFFSITE IMPACTS TO REPORT. THIS SITE IS A SECURE SITE AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC IS RESTRICTED FROM ENTRY. AS A RESULT OF THE WILDFIRE, EMPLOYEE ACCESS IS LIMITED.

Report Description
///WEB REPORT.///AT APPROXIMATELY 1130 SUNDAY, 12 JAN 2014, THE ANNISTON ARMY DEPOT (ANAD) FIRE DEPARTMENT RECEIVED A REPORT OF A RELEASE OF APPROXIMATELY 50 GALLONS OF UNUSED LIGHTWEIGHT 10W MOTOR OIL FROM A HOSE CONNECTED TO AN ABOVE-GROUND PRODUCT STORAGE TANK AT BUILDING 55 IN THE WEST AREA. DRK / HAZMAT SPILL RESPONSE PERSONNEL AND DPW ROADS AND GROUNDS WERE NOTIFIED AND RESPONDED TO CONTAIN AND CLEAN UP THE SPILL. WHILE MUCH OF THE AREA SURROUNDING THE TANK AT BUILDING 55 IS CONCRETED AND MOST OF THE SPILL WAS CONTAINED TO THE CONCRETE, APPROXIMATELY 5-15 GALLONS DID FLOW ONTO A DIRT BANK AND INTO AN ADJACENT DITCH, WHICH IS AN UNNAMED TRIBUTARY THAT FLOWS INTO EASTABOGA CREEK. A VISIBLE SHEEN WAS NOT NOTED IN THE DITCH AT THE INITIAL RESPONSE. ABSORBENT BOOMS WERE PLACED IN VARIOUS LOCATIONS ALONG THIS DITCH TO CAPTURE ANY OIL THAT MAY HAVE ESCAPED THE INITIAL CLEANUP, THE VACUUM TRUCK ON-SITE TO FACILITATE REMOVAL OF ANY OIL IN THE DITCH, AND THE IMPACTED DIRT CLEANED UP AND CONTAINERIZED IN A ROLL-OFF BOX FOR OFF-SITE DISPOSAL.

ABSORBENT BOOMS WERE PLACED IN VARIOUS LOCATIONS ALONG THIS DITCH TO CAPTURE ANY OIL THAT MAY HAVE ESCAPED THE INITIAL CLEANUP, THE VACUUM TRUCK ON-SITE TO FACILITATE REMOVAL OF ANY OIL IN THE DITCH, AND THE IMPACTED DIRT CLEANED UP AND CONTAINERIZED IN A ROLL-OFF BOX FOR OFF-SITE DISPOSAL.

properties.summary: Incident Type: AIRCRAFT - NRC Report ID: 835422 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: USCG AIR STATION LOS ANEGLES
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 835422
Incident Time: 2007-05-13 19:30:00
Nearest City: Seal Beach, CA
Incident Type: AIRCRAFT
Material: JET FUEL: JP-8
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: USCG AIR STATION LOS ANEGLES
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 45 gallons
///WEB REPORT/// COAST GUARD HELICOPTER 6588 WAS RESPONDING TO A MEDICAL VICTIM LOCATED ON THE SOUTHERN TIP OF THE LOS ALAMITOS BREAK WALL. IT WAS DETERMINED THAT THE 6588 WOULD BE HOISTING TWO PARAMEDICS AS WELL AS A POSSIBLE NECK/BACK INJURY PATIENT ON A LITTER. IN ORDER FOR THE 6588 TO COMPLETE THE HOISTS IT WAS NECESSARY TO JETTISON FUEL IN ORDER TO REDUCE AIRCRAFT WEIGHT. THE MEDICAL CONDITION OF THE VICTIM DID NOT ALLOW FOR FURTHER DELAY. 6588 PROCEEDED OFF SHORE AND JETTISONED APPROXIMATELY 45 GALLONS OF FUEL AT LOCATION N33-40 W118-07 (SE SAN PEDRO BAY). JETTISON VALVES WERE SECURED AND 6588 RETURNED TO COMPLETE THE HOISTING EVOLUTIONS OFF THE BREAK WALL. AS 6588 APPROACHED THE BREAK WALL, THE AIRCRAFT CAME TO A HOVER, RAISING THE NOSE OF THE AIRCRAFT AND CAUSING WHAT IS BELIEVED TO BE RESIDUAL FUEL IN THE JETTISON PIPING TO LEAVE THE AIRCRAFT. FROM VIDEO FOOTAGE IT APPEARS 10-15 GALLONS MAY HAVE LEFT THE AIRCRAFT FROM AN ALTITUDE OF APPROXIMATELY 75-100 !

THE RELEASE OF CHLORINATED WATER WAS DISCHARGED INTO A STORM WATER SYSTEM, WHICH LEADS TO THE FARMER'S BRANCH CREEK THEN GOES TO THE TRINITY RIVER. IT WAS REPORTED THAT AROUND 1000 DEAD FISH OF VARIOUS SPECIES WERE DISCOVERED AFTER THIS DISCHARGE. THE TARRANT REGIONAL WATER DISTRICT ADVISED THE CALLER OF THE DEAD FISH. SAMPLES WERE TAKEN OF THE FISH WHICH SHOWED SIGNS OF THE CHLORINATED WATER. THE CALLER STATED THAT THE WATER OPERATOR SHUT DOWN THE BACK FLOW PREVENTER AND THE UPSTREAM VALVE TO SECURE THE RELEASE. IT IS ESTIMATED THAT 5000 GALLONS OF CHLORINATED WATER WAS RELEASED INTO THE FARMER'S BRANCH CREEK.
